sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.10,50,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That on 14.10.2022 at about 05-30 p.m., when the petitioner was standing near Gundumgere cross bus stop, on Gowribidanur - Doddaballapura road, Tubgere hobli,
Doddaballapura Taluk, Bangalore Rural District, at that time, rider of Hero motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-50/EA-1851 rode the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
As a result of which, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body.

3. It is further stated that, immediately he was shifted to Nandi Hospital, for first aid,
thereafter he was shifted to Raksha Health Care Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and undergone surgery and spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards medicines,
attendant charges, food and nourishment etc.
4.

It is stated that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 42 years and doing coolie and also agriculture and earning Rs.30,000/-
per month.
Due to accidental injuries, he could not able to do his work as earlier.
5. It is stated that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of rider of the Hero motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-50/EA-1851.
Hence, Doddaballapura Rural Police have registered criminal case against rider of the offending vehicle in Crime No.258/2022.
As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation.
6. In response to issuance of notice, respondent No.1 & 2 were appeared through their respective counsel and filed written statements.
7. In the written statement, the respondent No.1 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further, admitted that he is the RC owner of the Hero motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-50/EA-1851 and same was insured with the respondent No.2.
The policy was in force as on the date of the accident and the rider had valid D.L..
It is the defence of the respondent that, this accident occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the petitioner and not on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.

Ultimately, stated that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive,
exaggerated and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

sentences.text: In the written statement, the respondent No.2 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further, denied about the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Hero motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-50/EA-1851.

It is also contention of the respondent that rider of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident,
hence there is a violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
It is the defence of the respondent that, this accident occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the petitioner and not on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
Ultimately, stated that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exaggerated and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

9. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following issues;
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 14.10.2022 at about 6.30 p.m. on Gowribidanuru-Doddaballapura road,
near Gundumgere cross bus stop, Tubgere hobli, Doddaballapura taluk, Bengaluru rural due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-  50-EA-1851 in an actionable  negligence?
2.
Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, at what rate and from whom?
3. What order or award?
10. In order to substantiate his case, the petitioner examined himself as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P21.
Apart from his evidence, placed the evidence of Dr.B.N.Nagaraj as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P22 & Ex.P23.

In addition to this placed the evidence of MRO of Raksha Hospital, Bangalore as PW3 and got marked Ex.P24 to Ex.P27.
11.
On the other hand, the respondents have not adduced any oral or documentary evidence on its behalf.

12. Heard the arguments of both the counsel and perused the materials available on record.
13.

My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order,

3  ISSUE No.1:-
14.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that due to actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the Hero motor cycle bearing registration No.KA- 50/EA-1851 the alleged accident had taken place,
consequently he had sustained grievous injuries.
15.

On the other hand, the respondents though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, but seriously disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
16. The petitioner in order to prove his case, got examined himself as PW1.
In his examination-in- chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of his oral evidence has relied upon Ex
. P1 to
Ex .P9 police documents

. Ex. P1-true copy of the F.I.R.
Ex.P2-true copy of first information statement, Ex.P3-true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P4-true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P5-true copy of spot sketch, Ex.P6- notice u/s 133 of MV Act, Ex.P7-reply to notice u/s 133 of MV Act, Ex.P8-true copy of IMV report and Ex.P9-true copy of charge sheet.

17. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by one Kempegowda, the S.H.O., Doddaballapura rural police station have registered the case in Cr.No.258/2022 against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC.

After completion of investigation, I.O. has filed the charge sheet against the rider of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/sec.279, 337 & 338 of IPC.
18.

The respondents though disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle, but not examined either the rider of the offending vehicle or any of the independent witness who witnessed the alleged accident to disprove the case of the petitioner.

19. Apart from this, even at the time of cross- examination of PW1, no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondents about the denial of allegation made against the rider of the offending vehicle.

20. In the light of the evidence placed on record, it is crystal clear that, the alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA- 50-EA-1851.
As such, the petitioner has placed satisfactory and convincing evidence on record to prove the above issue.
Hence, I am answering the issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2:
21.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.10,50,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

sentences.text:
Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injuries cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that, he has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries he has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P3.

The said document discloses that, he had sustained the following injuries:-
1) Type I open fracture tibia + plus (L)
2) cavlurian right shoulder 24.
In connection with the above said injuries the doctor is of the opinion that, the injury Nos. 1 to is grievous in nature and the injury No.2 is simple in nature.
The petitioner has produced discharge summary as per Ex.P10 issued by Raksha Health Care it discloses that he was admitted on 14.10.2022 and discharged on 17.10.2022.
In addition to his evidence, placed the evidence of Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW2.
PW2 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained type II fracture of the left tibia and fibula.
He has placed clinical note and x- ray at Ex.P22 & Ex.P23.
Further placed the evidence of MRO of Raksha Hospital, Bengaluru as PW3.
He has placed authorisation letter, requisition letter, postal acknowledgement, complaint copy at Ex.P24 to Ex.P27.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, he might have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an in patient as well as an outpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

Loss of income during treatment period:

sentences.text: PW1 has stated that, he was doing coolie and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
In this regard, he has placed RTC extracts and bank statement at Ex.P17 to Ex.P21.
But these documents does not show the exact income of the petitioner.
In the absence of the documents, it is apt to be considered notional income of the petitioner.
The petitioner has produced discharge summary as per Ex.P10 issued by Raksha Health Care it discloses that he was admitted on 14.10.2022 and discharged on 17.10.2022

As the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries definitely, there was some difficulty to him to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for a period of two months by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by him.

Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.31,000/-
towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Medical Expeneses;
26.
The petitioner in connection with his treatment expenses petitoner has produced medical bills of Rs.1,76,793/- as per Ex.P12 along with advance receipts and prescritpions at Ex.P13 & Ex.P14.
There are no contra materials available on record to show that the medical bills are created for the purpose of this case.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.1,76,793/- towards medical expenses.

Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
27.

The petitioner herein, as per the medical records, the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient and also as an outpatient, definitely the petitioner could have spent some amount towards,
food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,000/- towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.

Loss of future income;
28.
The petitioner herein, asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on his evidence along with the wound certificate and other medical documents.

In the evidence of the PW1,
reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.
As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him as per Ex.P3 goes to show that, he had sustained grievous injuries for which he took the treatment as an inpatient.
Apart from this, another material witness by name Dr.Nagaraj B.N. examined as PW2.
PW2 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained type II fracture of the left tibia and fibula.
For which, petitioner was underwent CRIF with IMIL nail for the left tibia on 14.10.2022.

Further, PW2 has stated that, at the time of examination of the petitioner for assessment of disability, the petitioner has wasting of left thig and calf muscles,
restricted left knee and ankle movements.
X-ray shows united fracture with implant in situ.
PW2 has assessed permanent physical disability of left lower limb at 45% and whole body is at 15%.

sentences.text: At the time of cross-examination of PW2, admitted that he is not the treated doctor.
And also admitted that fracture is united and implants in situ.
Further denied the suggestion that he assessed the disability of the petitioner on higher side to help the petitioner.
30. Over all appreciation of evidence of PW2 along with the entire medical documents the whole body disability expressed by PW2 as physical disability for limb is 45% and whole body is 15%.
Hence, by taking into consideration of point of disability expressed by PW2, it is apt to take whole body disability as 12% instead of 15%.
The same will meets the ends of justice.
31. In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 42 years.

In support of the age proof,
he has placed Aadhar card marked at Ex.P11 for consideration.

On going through the said document,
the date of birth of the petitioner has been mentioned as 15.2.1980.
The accident occurred on 14.10.2022.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the age of the petitioner is considered as 42 years.
To the said age as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '14' is to be taken into consideration.

32. Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in his evidence the petitioner has stated that, prior to the accident he was doing collie and agriculture and getting an income of Rs.30,000/- per month.
In this regard, he has placed RTC extracts and bank statement at Ex.P17 to Ex.P21.
But these documents does not show the exact income of the petitioner.
In the absence of the material documents, notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, in the case on hand, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2022.
As per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.15,500/- for the year 2022.

33. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner,
definitely come in the way of his future, in a slight manner, to do his daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood on going through his age criteria.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.15,500 X12 X 14 X 12/100= Rs.3,12,480/-.
Loss of amenities;
34.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accidental injuries, he cannot stand long time, lift weight and not in a position to do his profession.

On perusal of evidence of PW1 and PW2 and also medical documents, I am of the view that, the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also, to do his normal work, as well as his work for livelihood.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities.
PW2 has stated that petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants.
The estimate of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.
Relying on the opinion of the doctor it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.25,000/- under the head of future medication.

36. In view of my discussions held above, on various aspects the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
Compensation heads Compensation amount 1.Pain and Suffering Rs. 40,000-00 2.Loss of income during Rs. 31,000-00 laid-up period and rest period 3.

Medical expenses Rs.1,76,793-00 4. Attendant, Nourishment Rs. 5,000-00 and Conveyance Charges 5. Loss of future income Rs.3,12,480-00 due to disability 6. Loss of Amenities Rs. 20,000-00 7.Future medical expenses Rs. 25,000-00 Total Rs.6,10,273-00 37.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,10,273/- (Rupees six lakh ten thousand two hundred and seventy three only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016,
between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.

And MFA No.30131/2019 dated.12.5.2020, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount.
LIABILITY:
38.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-50-EA-1851 alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.
39. As per the records, the policy was valid from 14.3.2022 to 13.3.2023.
The alleged accident was taken place on 14.10.2022.

As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.

sentences.text: Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE N0.3:
40.

In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,10,273/- (Rupees six lakh ten thousand two hundred and seventy three only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondents are jointly and  severally liable to pay the compensation.

In  view of the valid insurance policy, the  respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
The expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.

After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
